title: Restriction normalization of the published open scalar conjugate
statement:
Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion of schemes [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $A_T=\Lambda_T$, $B_T=\Lambda'_T$, $T_T=B_T\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}-$, and let $\theta_j:T_Uj_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*T_X$ be the scalar-adjunction mate normalized by the balanced K-flat comparison [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], using the coefficient identifications of [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Let $\beta_j:T_Xj_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}T_U$ be precisely the conjugate defined in [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso] from the coefficient restriction square [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso]. Let $u_A:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j_A^*j_{!,A}$ and $u_B:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*j_{!,B}$ be the actual open adjunction units [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Then, naturally in every $M\in D(U,A_U)$,
$$u_{B,T_UM}^{-1}\circ j_B^*(\beta_{j,M})=T_U(u_{A,M}^{-1})\circ\theta_{j,j_{!,A}M}^{-1}.$$
This identifies the restriction of that specified conjugate, rather than choosing an independently normalized scalar-extension isomorphism. No flatness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $J_A=j_{!,A}$, $J_B=j_{!,B}$, $R_A=j_A^*$, $R_B=j_B^*$, and $r_T=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_T})$. The scalar adjunctions $T_T\dashv r_T$ are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]; denote their units by $\eta_T$. Denote the specified restriction square of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] by
$$c:r_UR_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Ar_X.$$
By [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso] the specified $\beta:T_XJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_U$ is its conjugate. In the convention of [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso], $\beta$ corresponds to $c$, with the adjunctions $J_BT_U\dashv r_UR_B$ and $T_XJ_A\dashv R_Ar_X$. Their Hom bijections are the successive individual Hom bijections, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Keep these adjunctions and the actual open units $u_A,u_B$ of the statement throughout.

source.place: Definition: conjugate along the two composite adjunctions

proof.text: We first check which action square $c$ represents. Put $F=j^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves, $\alpha_A=\alpha_j^\Lambda$, and $\alpha_B=\alpha_j^{\Lambda\prime}$. In this paragraph let $N$ be an ordinary $B_X$-module and use $R,r$ also for the ordinary pullback and scalar-restriction functors. In the pullback formula of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], identify $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_A}FN$ with $FN$ having action restricted along $\alpha_A^{-1}$, and likewise for $B$; these identifications are available because [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] makes both coefficient maps invertible. Using the coequalizer definition of extension in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], the identifications have balanced-tensor formulas $x\otimes n\mapsto\alpha_A^{-1}(x)n$ and $n\mapsto1\otimes n$. The action makes the first map balanced; its composite with the second is the identity, and the other composite is $x\otimes n\mapsto1\otimes\alpha_A^{-1}(x)n=x\otimes n$ by the balancing relation. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], $\alpha_B F(a_X)=a_U\alpha_A$, hence $\alpha_B^{-1}a_U=F(a_X)\alpha_A^{-1}$. Thus the actions on $r_U R_BN$ and $R_A r_XN$ coincide on the same object $FN$: both are restriction of the $F(B_X)$-action along this common composite. Here transporting an action and restricting it commute directly: for the monoidal structure $\mu$ of $F$, naturality gives $F(\gamma_N(a_X\otimes1))\mu=F\gamma_N\mu(F(a_X)\otimes1)$, using [sk-def-sfb-transport] and the restriction formula in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Both routes send a morphism $h$ to $Fh$.

source.place: Transport/restriction action calculation and coefficient-square calculation, written out

proof.text: The ordinary comparison [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso] is the composite of the transport/restriction comparison with the invertible coefficient-square comparison [def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso]. Unfold these specified comparisons using step 2: the transport comparison is the identity on $FN$, and the coefficient-square comparison, between the two tensor presentations, is the inverse collapse for $A$ after the collapse for $B$. On inverse-image modules its formula is consequently $n\mapsto n$; its inverse has the same formula. In particular this is precisely the action identification, with no automorphism of $FN$ inserted. The square [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] is the levelwise version of this comparison. In every degree the above formulas and their inverses commute with the differential, since they commute with every module morphism. Applying the localization functor preserves these equalities and inverse identities. Therefore on the derived categories, after the coefficient identifications used in the statement, $c^{-1}:R_Ar_X\to r_UR_B$ is exactly the action identification whose scalar-adjunction mate is $\theta_j$ in [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization].

source.place: Final displayed composite; derived levelwise construction in def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso.md

proof.text:
For $M\in D(U,A_U)$ put $V=J_AM$ and $N=J_BT_UM$. Transpose $\beta_M:T_XV\to N$ under the composite $T_XJ_A\dashv R_Ar_X$. The result is $R_Ar_X(\beta_M)\circ R_A(\eta_{X,V})\circ u_{A,M}$, by the composite-unit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. On the other hand, $1_N$ transposes under $J_BT_U\dashv r_UR_B$ to $r_U(u_{B,T_UM})\circ\eta_{U,M}$. By the defining Hom correspondence of [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso], postcomposition of this second transpose by $c_N$ is the first transpose: precomposition of $1_N$ by the specified conjugate $\beta_M$ is $\beta_M$. Consequently
$$R_Ar_X(\beta_M)\circ R_A(\eta_{X,V})\circ u_{A,M}
=c_N\circ r_U(u_{B,T_UM})\circ\eta_{U,M}.\tag{1}$$
This uses the actual conjugate specified in [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso], rather than choosing another isomorphism between the same left adjoints.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints: defining Hom correspondence; composite units expanded as in Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits

proof.text:
The K-flat lemma concerns sectionwise module sheaves; transport it along the underlying-sheaf-preserving equivalences $E_T$ with module objects. They identify $T_T$, $r_T$ and the specified derived scalar adjunctions (unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$) by [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction], and $R_A,R_B$ with the sectionwise pullbacks along $j^{-1}\Lambda_{X,\mathrm{sec}}\cong\Lambda_{U,\mathrm{sec}}$ induced by $\alpha$ by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. These comparisons send generators to generators, so after the collapses of step 2 they are the identity on $FN$: $c^{-1}$ corresponds to the lemma's identification $h_A^*r_Y=r_Xh_B^*$ for $h=j^{-1}$, rings identified by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], and the mate is taken under the adjunctions $T\dashv r$ of steps 1 and 6. By [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] and step 3, the specified $\theta_V:T_UR_AV\to R_BT_XV$ is the scalar-adjunction mate of $c^{-1}$. Its transpose under $T_U\dashv r_U$ is therefore
$$r_U(\theta_V)\circ\eta_{U,R_AV}
=c^{-1}_{T_XV}\circ R_A(\eta_{X,V}).\tag{2}$$
Indeed, the inverse-mates formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] inserts the scalar unit on the $X$ side, applies $c^{-1}$, and then contracts the $U$-scalar counit; transposing contracts that counit with its unit and leaves exactly the displayed right side. The K-flat normalization lemma identifies this mate with the balanced tensor comparison on the entire ordinary unbounded derived category and says it is invertible without flatness of $a$. Thus (2) is available at the possibly unbounded object $V=J_AM$, and $\theta_V^{-1}$ is the specified inverse.

source.place: (1) balanced K-flat comparison, applied to j; scalar mate expanded by its unit/counit formula

proof.text:
Set $d=R_B(\beta_M)\circ\theta_V\circ T_U(u_{A,M}):T_UM\to R_BJ_BT_UM$. Under $T_U\dashv r_U$ from [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], its transpose is $r_U(d)\circ\eta_{U,M}$. Naturality of $\eta_U$ at $u_{A,M}$, then (2), gives
$$\begin{aligned}
r_U(d)\eta_{U,M}
&=r_UR_B(\beta_M)\,r_U(\theta_V)\eta_{U,R_AV}\,u_{A,M}\\
&=r_UR_B(\beta_M)\,c^{-1}_{T_XV}\,R_A(\eta_{X,V})\,u_{A,M}\\
&=c_N^{-1}\,R_Ar_X(\beta_M)\,R_A(\eta_{X,V})\,u_{A,M}\\
&=r_U(u_{B,T_UM})\eta_{U,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is naturality of $c^{-1}$ at $\beta_M:T_XV\to N$; the last line substitutes (1) and cancels $c_N^{-1}c_N$. The final expression is exactly the transpose of $u_{B,T_UM}$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection yields
$$R_B(\beta_M)\circ\theta_V\circ T_U(u_{A,M})=u_{B,T_UM}.\tag{3}$$

source.place: (2), alternative common-right-adjoint argument: explicit equality of scalar transposes

proof.text:
The units $u_A,u_B$ are the invertible open units specified in the statement, and $\theta$ is invertible by step 5. Postcompose (3) by $u_{B,T_UM}^{-1}$, then precompose by $T_U(u_{A,M}^{-1})\circ\theta_V^{-1}$. Functoriality gives $T_U(u_{A,M})T_U(u_{A,M}^{-1})=1$, so
$$u_{B,T_UM}^{-1}\circ R_B(\beta_M)=T_U(u_{A,M}^{-1})\circ\theta_V^{-1},\qquad V=J_AM,$$
which is the required formula. Every transformation used above is natural and all equations hold for arbitrary $M$, so this is a natural identity. Only the invertibility already specified for the open units and the unbounded K-flat normalization are used; no flatness or boundedness hypothesis has entered.
